Team / Rajiv,

Following our last sync, I've sketched a concrete deployment sequence for the Private (VPC) minor version refresh (v2.8.3 -> v2.9.0) and a short rollback rehearsal we want to run with Acme's CloudOps during the maintenance window. Goal: validate version pinning behavior, KV cache warmup expectations, and a safe rollback path that preserves customer-configured model pins.

High-level plan (attached runbook):
- Nightly blue/green patch of non-critical zones (staging-like traffic) for 2 nights to validate kernels and quantization profiles.
- Single-region maintenance window (primary VPC subnet) on Friday 2026-12-11 01:00-03:00 UTC for canary -> gradual ramp -> full cutover.
- Rolling restart of serving runtime with pinned model versions; fallback policy to prior quantized variant if any perf or correctness regressions detected.
- Pre-cutover checks: snapshot of KV caches, API health probes, token-cost smoke tests, and audit log export.
- Rollback rehearsal: simulate a performance regression at 02:10 UTC; execute rollback steps and measure time-to-recover (target < 8 minutes).

Open questions for Acme:
1) Are the proposed windows acceptable for your on-call rota?
2) Can CloudOps run the rollback trigger (we'll provide the runbook snippet and a signed SSO link)?
3) Any additional compliance evidence you need captured during rehearsal (audit log retention, signed timestamps)?

Please see the attached runbook and the checklist. Dev, can you confirm the model-pinning semantics for autoscaled nodes (particularly how the runtime handles mixed-quantization caches during partial rollouts)? Vivek / Lauren — if this looks ok from an ops/leadership standpoint, I'll lock the plan and circulate to legal for a short maintenance notice.

Thanks,
Soojin
Soojin Lee

Thanks Soojin — quick technical notes on the plan:

- Model-pinning and mixed-quantization: the runtime guarantees pinning at the routing layer; however during rolling upgrades you'll see nodes serving a mix of quantized and full-precision variants until the node pool is homogeneous. We rely on prefix KV cache compatibility — for v2.9.0 we added a small version-tag to KV keys to prevent silent cache corruption.

- Rollback mechanics: rollback is a two-step process: (1) route traffic back to the prior model variant via routing policy (fast, atomic), (2) downscale upgraded nodes (graceful termination) and re-provision older image. If the routing rollback is sufficient we won't need full reprovisioning. Time-to-route-change ~30s; reprovisioning variable (3-10m).

- Observability hooks: I added a temporary probe that checks token latency percentiles and generation divergence against a small reference prompt set — this will flip 'failure' if latency SLO or divergence thresholds are exceeded. We'll surface this in the Console and via PagerDuty.

Action items for me before rehearsal:
- Add the KV key versioning note to the runbook (done, v1.1).
- Create the canary traffic script (will be under the Drive link).
- Provide the routing rollback play snippet (I can demo during the rehearsal).

I'll be available during the window.

- Dev
